UnitStatement: Build And Release Guide
This guide defines the provider-neutral build, packaging, and release-evidence skeleton for OpenPipeStress.
The guide gives maintainers a reproducible local path for collecting software-quality evidence before a future CI provider, release matrix, signing process, and publishing workflow are selected.

This guide is not a live CI workflow, release publication authorization, professional engineering approval, legal opinion, certification, sealing, standards-body endorsement, or code-compliance determination.
The current implementation lane is provider-neutral.
Hosted CI is deferred by human ruling DEC-025 (2026-06-11, recorded in execution/_Decomposition/SOFTWARE_DECOMP.md §12).
The five-surface local evidence sweep (§5.1) is the commit-bound merge gate for parallel agent development branches.
Hosted CI is re-decided at the named follow-up D-05b (public sanitized-export CI, prepared with D-06).
GitHub Actions on the private monorepo remains prohibited absent an explicitly recorded §7 private-data-handling authorization.
No .github/ or other live workflow file is created by this deliverable.
No installer, signed binary, notarized package, attestation, or publication target is generated.
No final OS/architecture release matrix is selected.
No final numerical tolerance, coverage, performance, or maintainer-quorum threshold is selected.
Those decisions remain TBD until a human project authority records them.
The current repository has a root npm workspace manifest (package.json with the apps/desktop workspace).
The repository has a Tauri 2 desktop shell under apps/desktop/ (apps/desktop/package.json and apps/desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml).
There is still no root Cargo workspace; Rust crates remain crate-local under core/, validation/benchmarks/, and apps/desktop/src-tauri/.
Python tests and validation helpers live under tests/ and tools/.
The provider-neutral readiness script discovers existing manifests instead of assuming a future workspace layout.
The browser-mode operation engine is the wasm32 build of core/model_operations/operation_applier (DEC-020 / ADR-0001).
Building the desktop app for browser-mode use requires the wasm32-unknown-unknown Rust target and the wasm-bindgen CLI at exactly the version pinned in that crate's Cargo.toml.
The wasm artifact is produced by `npm run build:wasm --workspace apps/desktop`, generated under apps/desktop/src/services/wasmEngine/__generated__/, and never committed.
The build script fails with explicit remediation commands when a prerequisite is missing.
The wasm build writes glue to a sibling temp directory and renames it into place, so a concurrent reader never sees a half-written artifact set (DEC-025 F-4 rider).
Readiness check commands: `python3 tools/release/check_release_readiness.py --profile skeleton` (also with --execute), `--profile cargo`, and `--profile all`.
Without --execute, check_release_readiness.py performs path checks and prints the local commands it would run.
With --execute, check_release_readiness.py runs only local commands from the selected profile.
check_release_readiness.py does not use network services, release signing, publication credentials, or shell command evaluation.
A release-evidence record should capture the source revision as a Git commit hash or explicit working-tree state.
A release-evidence record should capture working tree state: clean, or a list of changed files if evidence is pre-commit.
A release-evidence record should capture runtime versions: Python, Cargo/Rust, and Node/package tooling where applicable.
A release-evidence record should capture commands run: exact command, profile, host OS, and pass/fail result.
A release-evidence record should capture artifacts reviewed: docs, schemas, binaries, packages, manifests, or reports.
A release-evidence record should capture validation status: the applicable release-quality gate outcome or waiver.
A release-evidence record should capture data boundary status: protected-content, private-data, and real-secret scan result.
A release-evidence record should capture known limitations: open risks and unresolved TBD decisions.
A release-evidence record should capture the human gate: maintainer or project-authority acceptance record, if any.
Working-tree evidence may support review, but release publication should bind to a committed source revision unless a human release authority records an exception.
The local readiness script defines provider-neutral check profiles.
Profile `skeleton`: documentation path checks, dependency schema validation, and focused script tests; a fast smoke check for the release skeleton.
Profile `python`: Python contract, governance, and validation tests; the local Python gate before review.
Profile `security`: security/privacy tests; the local privacy and redaction gate.
Profile `cargo`: `cargo test` for discovered crate manifests; the local Rust crate gate without a root workspace assumption.
Profile `all`: union of available local profiles; a maintainer pre-release dry run or local full run.
The final CI job names, matrix, required thresholds, and failure policy remain TBD.
Future provider-specific workflows should call the same local script or an equivalent command plan so local and hosted evidence stay comparable.
The deterministic local evidence entrypoint is `python3 tools/release/run_evidence_sweep.py` (dry-run prints the plan; --execute runs the sweep).
The evidence sweep runs the five evidence surfaces sequentially in a fixed F-4-safe order, failing fast and recording later surfaces as not_run.
Surface 1 of the sweep is the Rust crate sweep: `python3 tools/release/check_release_readiness.py --profile cargo --execute`.
Surface 2 of the sweep is Python tests: `python3 -m pytest -q tests`.
Surface 3 of the sweep is Desktop Vitest with the wasm engine built first: `npm run build:wasm:desktop` then `npm run test:desktop`.
Surface 4 of the sweep is Playwright e2e: `npm run test:e2e:desktop`.
Surface 5 of the sweep is the desktop production build: `npm run build:desktop`.
Each execute run writes a machine-readable summary artifact to validation/evidence/sweeps/SWEEP_<utc>_<commit12>[-dirty].json.
The sweep summary artifact contains the bound commit hash, branch, working-tree deltas, runtime versions, per-command exit codes and durations, and the overall pass/fail status.
The sweep exit code is 0 only when all five surfaces pass.
Merge-gate role (DEC-025): the sweep is the required pre-push/fan-in evidence for every parallel agent development branch.
Recommended gate pattern step 1: commit the completed tranche.
Recommended gate pattern step 2: run `python3 tools/release/run_evidence_sweep.py --execute` at the clean committed HEAD so the summary binds to that commit hash.
Recommended gate pattern step 3: commit the summary artifact as an evidence-only closeout commit and push.
A dirty-tree sweep is recorded as working-tree evidence: the summary lists the deltas and the filename carries a -dirty suffix.
Per §4, a dirty-tree sweep may support review, but the merge gate binds to a clean committed revision.

The surfaces must not run concurrently with each other or with a second sweep on the same checkout: surfaces 3 and 4 rebuild the shared wasm engine artifact and the cargo sweep saturates the same cores.
The atomic wasm-build swap (§3) removes the half-written-artifact hazard, not the contention.

A green sweep is development evidence only; it is not a release claim, release publication authorization, professional engineering approval, certification, sealing, authentication, or code-compliance determination.
The current packaging skeleton is a checklist, not a package build.
Packaging checklist step 1: confirm source revision and working-tree state.
Packaging checklist step 2: run applicable local readiness profiles.
Packaging checklist step 3: confirm release quality gates in docs/RELEASE_QUALITY_GATES.md.
Packaging checklist step 4: confirm protected-content, private-data, and real-secret scan disposition.
Packaging checklist step 5: prepare release notes from docs/RELEASE_NOTES_TEMPLATE.md.
Packaging checklist step 6: record known limitations, unresolved TBD decisions, and human gate state.
Packaging checklist step 7: if binaries or installers are later produced, record package path, target, build command, checksum, signing/notarization state, and publication state.
Desktop packaging is expected to follow the accepted Tauri-supported macOS/Windows/Linux architecture baseline when a GUI package exists.
Exact target triples, installer formats, signing identities, notarization process, and publication destinations remain TBD.
Hosted CI is deferred (DEC-025; re-decided at D-05b with D-06).

When a hosted location is later selected, the provider workflow should map to stable phases, with the five-surface sweep (§5.1) as the local command basis so local and hosted evidence stay comparable.
Future CI phase Repository sanity maps to `python3 tools/release/check_release_readiness.py --profile skeleton --execute`.
Future CI phase Python/schema contracts maps to `python3 tools/release/check_release_readiness.py --profile python --execute`.
Future CI phase Security/privacy checks maps to `python3 tools/release/check_release_readiness.py --profile security --execute`.
Future CI phase Rust crates maps to `python3 tools/release/check_release_readiness.py --profile cargo --execute`.
Future CI phase Release candidate review maps to release notes, gate record, scan record, and human acceptance record.

Hosted CI must not receive private project data, private rule packs, private material/component libraries, protected standards content, signing secrets, or publishing credentials unless a later security and release-governance decision explicitly authorizes that handling.
Every release candidate record should identify the source revision and evidence profile.
Every release candidate record should identify changed packages and deliverables.
Every release candidate record should identify checks and gate outcomes.
Every release candidate record should identify package or artifact paths, if generated.
Every release candidate record should identify checksums for generated artifacts, if any.
Every release candidate record should identify validation status and known limitations.
Every release candidate record should identify data-boundary and professional-boundary notices.
Every release candidate record should identify the human review or waiver record.
Release labels describe software maturity and validation evidence; they do not approve a project-specific piping calculation, authenticate a user rule pack, or replace competent professional review.

Decided 2026-06-11 (DEC-025): hosted CI deferred; the five-surface local sweep (§5.1) is the commit-bound merge gate; hosted workflow location is re-decided at D-05b (public sanitized-export CI, prepared with D-06).
